extracted.intended_audience: Biomedical researchers applying for NIH grants (K, R, R21, R01, R15, SBIR) and investigators seeking funding/advice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and informal standards for preparing, submitting, and managing NIH grant applications, plus procedural timelines (JIT, Council, NoA), eligibility rules (ESI/new investigator, multi-PI), and interactions with Program Officers and Grants Management Specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESI / New Investigator applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI (and New investigator, where recognized) only applies to R01 applications – no other activity codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESI/new investigator status gives a payline break for R01s; it does not apply to R21 or R03. Preserve ESI status for resubmissions (status active as of submission date). If in doubt, confirm with your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-PI effect on New Investigator benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application includes an established PI, the application will not qualify for any of the new investigator benefits... It qualifies only if all the PIs are new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple-PI applications only retain new investigator benefits if all PIs are new. Once a multiple-PI application is funded, the new PI(s) lose their new PI status. Consider PI/co-I roles strategically on resubmissions to protect ESI status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of New Investigator status when taking over existing R01
rubrics_metrics.description: If your institution assigns you to become a principal investigator (PI) on an existing grant that you did not apply for, you still qualify as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH policy allows taking over an R01 without losing new investigator status because you didn't compete for the award. Confirm with your IC/PO if unsure, since local interpretation can vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity-code specificity for ESI benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: ESI (and New investigator, where recognized) only applies to R01 applications – no other activity codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect ESI/NI concessions (payline advantage, different reviewer expectations) on R21, R03, or other non-R01 activity codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline and select-pay understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines vary by IC and FY; last year's payline does not guarantee current-year payline. POs may advocate for select pay but it is not common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for changing paylines (they can be cut). If your score is near the payline, ask your PO about select-pay possibilities after you receive the summary statement. Programmatic discretion can sometimes result in funding above the published payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact your Program Officer (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the PO after receiving the summary statement to discuss next steps; but allow reasonable time for PO response (more than a week). Provide specific questions or request a call with topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs have heavy portfolios; include specific questions to make meetings productive. If no response in a couple of weeks and the question is time-sensitive, escalate to the PO’s supervisor (branch/division chief). For high scores or JIT requests, contacting the PO earlier is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: How POs can help and their limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: POs can give insight, attend study sections (without contributing to reviews), and advocate programmatically, but they cannot unilaterally change review outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POs may provide interpretation of reviews and advise on resubmission strategies; they triage many tasks and may be slow to respond. Use PO input strategically (study section choice, resubmission planning, eligibility questions).

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT (Just-in-Time) and Grants Management Specialist (GMS) process
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending administrative review / JIT requests are part of pre-award processing; after submitting JIT items the award may be prepared and NoA released about a month later in typical cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you receive a JIT request, submit requested documents promptly. 'Pending' status is generally good news when score is below payline; there's usually no need to ask PO/GMS whether you will be funded if you are below payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing revision/supplement eligibility requirement (parent award term)
rubrics_metrics.description: This FOA will utilize the R01 mechanism and targets currently funded R01 projects with at least two years left at the estimated time of award. Applicants cannot request funds beyond the end date of the parent award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing revisions (supplements) require the parent award to have sufficient remaining time; if your active R01 expires before the supplement award would end, you are ineligible. Verify FOA-specific eligibility language and consult the PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using R21 funds for equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use R21 funds for small equipment (under $60K) if the FOA has no restriction, but it will eat a significant portion of the budget for a two-year R21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may be dubious if an R21 looks like an equipment grant. Consider context and justification; discuss with your PO to determine how it will be perceived in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting SBIR Phase II with contract research organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: For services like GLP NHP tox studies done by Charles River, you can budget them as fee-for-service rather than as a subcontract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifying a vendor as fee-for-service may affect indirect cost calculations (some PIs exclude fee-for-service amounts from indirect cost base). Confirm with PO and institutional grants office for proper budget treatment and IDC calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section selection and referral strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify appropriate SRGs/study sections (disease-focused vs methodology) and, if needed, ask SROs about receptivity; use Matchmaker/ART tools to find suitable panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the application narrative to the chosen study section's priorities. Sending aims to potential new SROs to get buy-in can reduce the chance of your application being inappropriately assigned. Reassigning to a different study section has successfully improved scores for some applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicts / biased reviewers and PHS referral requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If you believe a study section contains reviewers with conflicts or competing interests, you can indicate concerns in a PHS referral/request form and provide publications/grant examples showing direct competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objective evidence to justify referral requests. Also consider re-directing your application to a different SRG where the work will be appreciated rather than judged by competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to repeated/new criticisms across resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated unscored reviews that raise new, unrelated criticisms are frustrating; strategies include moving the submission to another study section, improving narrative on significance, and consulting PO for next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewer concerns are clear and addressable, A1 resubmissions often improve scores. Consider an independent naive reader to ensure the significance and narrative are clear to non-experts in your immediate niche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategy (A0 -> A1) expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is common to drop from higher scores to within funding range from the A0 to A1, especially if the reviewer concerns are clear and easily addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After summary statement, discuss with your PO whether to resubmit. Address reviewer critiques directly and focus on clarity and feasible experiments to improve percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: RF1 vs R01 change does not imply re-review
rubrics_metrics.description: An application ID change from R01 to RF1 likely reflects an administrative/activity-code change; RF1 is an all-purpose multi-year award activity code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a switch usually does not mean you will undergo a second review. Ask your PO for clarification if concerned, but do not assume re-review is imminent based solely on an ID change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and interpretation of Council review / paylines posting
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs often wait until many applications have been reviewed before publicly updating paylines; Council review completion does not guarantee immediate award action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your status is 'Council review completed' and you received JIT requests, that's a positive sign. Expect internal ranking discussions and possible delays; ask PO whether to prepare JIT if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-funding nominations (e.g., OBSSR) are selective and slow
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-funding nominations by an IC (e.g., OBSSR) are relatively rare and selective; nomination is positive but may take months to finalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being nominated indicates strong scientific merit; monitor timelines and stay in touch with the PO for status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start date conventions and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical project start dates vary by review cycle (e.g., April 1 for some awards; July start dates may apply to other cycles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the expected start date for your award; do not assume a July start for all cases. If you have employment changes, POs can approve delaying start dates or transferring the award to a new institution with documentation of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: When JIT revisions indicate positive funding likelihood
rubrics_metrics.description: PO/GMS requests to revise documents (e.g., data sharing plan) and subsequent Pending status are indicators of likely funding when score is below payline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit requested revisions quickly. If below payline and JIT requested, asking whether you will be funded is often unnecessary—the processing is underway; allow time for NoA issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing between R21 and R01 as an early-career applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: R21s are not effective starter grants for new investigators in many cases; R21 success rates are often higher for established investigators using them per intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a new investigator, consider applying for an R01 or specific mechanisms intended to support new investigators rather than relying on R21 as a starter grant. Discuss options with your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO responsiveness expectations and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs should not expect immediate replies; wait longer than a week for a substantive reply. If no response, follow up or contact the PO’s supervisor for time-sensitive matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, specific questions in emails to POs to get actionable responses. If you need quick guidance for submission timing, it's acceptable to ask whether you should submit an A1 in the upcoming cycle.
